subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these goal records.

judge.implied_focus: The nature and quality of each goal's improvement intervention -- i.e., characterizing what kind of change each goal represents and how well-specified/measurable it is.

per_column.name: intervention_type
per_column.rationale: Classifies the kind of improvement lever each goal pursues -- a core facet of characterizing the intervention behind a goal.

per_column.name: scope_of_change
per_column.rationale: Captures breadth/reach of the intervention (company-wide vs team), a coherent facet of the same focus.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Temporal dimension of the goal/intervention; sensible facet for prioritizing attention.

per_column.name: measurement_approach
per_column.rationale: How the goal is measured -- ties directly to whether a goal is trackable, part of characterizing worth-of-attention.

per_column.name: metric_category_alignment
per_column.rationale: Quality/consistency flag on whether metric matches category; contributes to assessing goal rigor, adjacent to the focus.

per_column.name: baseline_state_specified
per_column.rationale: Measurability/completeness flag indicating whether progress can be judged -- supports the 'worth attention' quality angle.

per_column.name: category_specific_lever
per_column.rationale: Finer-grained lever within category; a deeper facet of intervention characterization, though partially overlaps intervention_type.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on a coherent inferred focus: characterizing each goal's improvement intervention along several facets (type, scope, time horizon, measurement) plus data-quality/specification flags (metric-category alignment, baseline specified). This is not a scattered grab-bag; the facets are complementary and cohere around 'what kind of change is this goal and is it well-specified/measurable.' Structure is sound and multi-faceted at a useful granularity, mixing categorical typologies with binary rigor flags, giving a genuine analytical decomposition rather than a single restatement. There is mild redundancy between intervention_type and category_specific_lever, and the two boolean flags lean toward a data-quality sub-theme that is slightly distinct from the intervention-characterization theme, which prevents top marks on coherence. The implied focus is actionable: an analyst can prioritize goals by scope, horizon, measurement rigor, and baseline availability to decide 'what's worth attention.' None of the columns are mechanical/generic (no token counts or bare sentiment), so the claim is substantively realised.
